card.name: Red Porch House with Yard Swing
card.summary: A two-storey red shingle-clad house featuring a large front porch and a yard swing.
card.description: This residence presents a bold, saturated red facade that commands attention from the street, clad entirely in durable asphalt shingles that provide a textured, layered appearance. The structure rises two stories, offering a substantial footprint that balances the expansive front porch with the private spaces within. The porch is a defining feature, extending significantly from the main volume to create a sheltered outdoor living area, supported by sturdy columns that echo the vertical lines of the windows. The roofline is pitched, covered in matching shingles to maintain a cohesive monochromatic aesthetic, while the large windows on both levels allow natural light to penetrate the interior. The yard is open and uncluttered, save for a single swing set that adds a playful, domestic touch to the otherwise formal exterior. The red color is consistent across all visible surfaces, from the siding to the porch railings, creating a unified visual statement. The scale is generous, with wide doorways and deep eaves that provide shade and character. The overall impression is one of solidity and warmth, a home that feels both inviting and established, with the swing in the yard suggesting a space designed for relaxation and leisure. The shingle material ensures low maintenance and weather resistance, while the two-storey design maximizes living space on the lot.
plan: Survey the empty lot to determine the optimal orientation for the house and the placement of the yard swing.
Draft the architectural plans for a two-storey structure with a large front porch, specifying the red shingle cladding.
Pour the concrete foundation and install the floor joists for the first and second stories.
Erect the wooden frame and apply the red shingle siding to the exterior walls and roof.
Install the windows, doors, and the structural supports for the large front porch.
Construct the yard swing set in the open space and perform a final inspection of the red finish and structural integrity.
assumptions: The house is assumed to be a two-storey colonial style based on the reference designs and the 'two' in the brief.
The 'big porch' is interpreted as a covered front porch extending significantly from the main facade.
The 'yard swing' is assumed to be a standard residential swing set located in the front yard.
The interior layout is assumed to include three bedrooms and one bathroom, typical for a two-storey home of this size.
